entries.what_happened: Four of the five manuscripts claim the rational Hodge conjecture (HC) for specified classes of varieties; the fifth is a conditional reduction and proves no HC case. (1) 'The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties' (6 Oct) claims that for every complex CM abelian variety A and every p, the cycle class map CH^p(A)_Q -> H^{2p}(A,Q) ∩ H^{p,p}(A) is surjective (Theorem thm:cm), hence HC in every codimension on every finite product of CM abelian varieties and on their powers. It also claims the generalized HC for CM abelian varieties (Corollary cc:ghc), via Hazama and Abdulali. The proof is a Hodge-theoretic construction: theta one-forms on a compact ball quotient, Hecke and Frobenius arithmetic, and a four-factor surface criterion. (2) 'Weil classes and Hodge classes on abelian powers' (6 Oct) claims HC in every codimension on every self-power A^m, m >= 1, for two classes: complex abelian sixfolds with an imaginary-quadratic action whose rational Hermitian form is hyperbolic of signature (3,3) (Theorem p3ab:split-sixfolds), and complex abelian varieties of dimension at most five with an imaginary-quadratic action (Theorem p3ab:quadratic-five). Both allow nonsimple varieties and special periods. Its key tensor criterion (Theorem p3:tensor-criterion) reduces Hodge tensors to determinant lines supplied by CM cycles and by a Weil-plane input (Theorem p3sw:weil-plane), which the text proves by following Markman's construction. (3) 'Abelian covers, Gale correspondences, and the Hodge conjecture for powers' (6 Oct) claims HC in every codimension for (i) self-powers of the Jacobian of a connected abelian cover of curves at each point s of a complement of a countable union of proper closed analytic subsets of the marked parameter space, and for products of such a Jacobian with a CM abelian variety (Theorem p4:abelian-covers); and (ii) self-powers of very general smooth diagonal complete intersections X_A in P^{d+c} of dimension d, cut out by c <= 2 equations of common degree n >= 2, for every d (Theorem thm:main). (4) 'Algebraic Kuga-Satake correspondences and Hodge conjectures on a K3 quadratic locus' (30 Sep) claims HC and the generalized HC in every degree for every self-power S^m of a projective K3 surface S that admits a rational isometric embedding (T_S,q) into V_P, with V_P = U_Q^{+2} ⊥ <-1>^4 (Theorem main:theorem). This includes every ample P-polarized K3, P = U ⊕ D8(-1) ⊕ D4(-1). It also states the general criterion (Theorem ext:criterion): algebraicity of one exact even-Clifford Kuga-Satake tensor on any projective K3 implies HC and GHC for every self-power. Corollary transfer:moduli extends these to Hilbert schemes of points and certain moduli spaces. (5) 'A Conditional Reduction for Algebraic Kuga-Satake Correspondences' (10 Sep) proves no HC case. At a K3 point with full orthogonal Hodge group, existence of any one nonzero algebraic correspondence from primitive H^2 of the K3 to H^2 of an abelian variety is equivalent to algebraicity of the prescribed full Kuga-Satake correspondence (Theorem main:generic). If that existence holds very generally in a polarized component, the prescribed correspondence is algebraic throughout the component (Theorem main:specialization). The existence input is stated as unproven.
entries.delivers: Establishes HC (rational coefficients, algebraic cycle classes, every degree) only for the listed classes: CM abelian varieties and their finite products and powers; all self-powers of the split (3,3) sixfolds and of abelian varieties of dimension at most five with an imaginary-quadratic action; all self-powers of abelian-cover Jacobians at generic markings, and of their products with CM abelian varieties; self-powers of very general diagonal complete intersections of the stated type; all self-powers of K3 surfaces with a rational isometric embedding of T_S into V_P, plus Hilbert schemes and moduli spaces of those K3s. Since dim V_P = 8, that hypothesis forces rank T_S <= 8, i.e. Picard number >= 14 (my reading of the hypothesis). The generalized HC is claimed only for CM abelian varieties and for the K3 self-powers (including Hilbert schemes and moduli spaces); the other manuscripts claim HC alone. The manuscripts do not claim to settle the general problem as the bullet states it (every smooth projective complex X, any dimension, any degree). For the CM paper, the statement matches the list's (rational coefficients, complex-subvariety cycles, all degrees) but restricted to CM abelian varieties. The Sept 10 manuscript delivers no unconditional HC result.
entries.remains: HC for smooth projective complex varieties in general. For abelian varieties: all non-CM ones outside the listed quadratic-action and (3,3)-sixfold classes, including general abelian varieties of dimension six or more. For K3 surfaces: those whose transcendental quadratic space does not rationally embed in V_P, unless the criterion's exact tensor is shown algebraic. For abelian-cover Jacobians: the non-generic markings. For diagonal complete intersections with c = 2: the exceptional locus, per the theorem's statement. The generalized HC beyond the listed cases. The existence of the initial Kuga-Satake correspondence at any point, which the Sept 10 manuscript leaves as the external input.
entries.direction: proves the conjecture for special classes of varieties (CM abelian varieties; several families of self-powers); conditional reduction for Kuga-Satake algebraicity
entries.object: No counterexample. The Gale correspondence in the diagonal complete intersection manuscript is an explicit algebraic correspondence (a perfect tensor between the two character spaces, pulled back to a Fermat hypersurface F_n^{m-2}). The cycles for CM classes are not written out: they come from a compact ball-quotient construction and an existence-type surface criterion. The K3 correspondence Gamma_S is built from double covers of abelian surfaces, Gauss pencils and a degree-three Hodge comparison, not written down explicitly.
entries.conditional_on: Within this family: the CM Hodge theorem (Theorem thm:cm of 'The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties', cited as OpenAICM2026 or OpenAICM) is the only Hodge-conjecture input of 'Weil classes and Hodge classes on abelian powers' (its Lemma p3:cm-operations) and of 'Abelian covers, Gale correspondences...' (through its companion results). The abelian-cover manuscript also uses the companion results of the Weil manuscript (its Section 2 tools, Theorem 2.5 saturated criterion, Lemma 2.6 correspondence transfer; the text says 'their proofs belong to the companion paper'). The Weil manuscript's Weil-plane input (Theorem p3sw:weil-plane) is proved in the text, but it follows Markman's construction and cites Markman's lemmas (Markman 2025, Section 7.4.2 and Lemmas 9.3.2, 9.3.11; Markman 2026, Sections 11.3-11.5), plus Buchweitz-Flenner and Caldararu-type Hochschild results. The abelian-cover exceptional loci rely on Cattani-Deligne-Kaplan (algebraicity of Hodge loci, arXiv 1994) and on Shioda-Katsura Fermat domination. The K3 manuscript relies on external results: Buskin (algebraicity of rational Hodge isometries of K3 surfaces), Varesco (powers of K3 surfaces and similarities), Zarhin, and, for Corollary transfer:moduli, de Cataldo-Migliorini, Bulles, Arapura and Riess. Its conditional criterion (Theorem ext:criterion) needs one exact cycle; Theorem main:theorem supplies that cycle on the V_P locus. The Sept 10 manuscript is conditional on the existence of one very generally nonzero algebraic correspondence, which it calls the external existence problem. The CM manuscript's specialization remark depends on a separate companion, 'Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties' (7 Oct), which I did not read; the text says that remark is not an input to the main theorem.
entries.doubts: The CM manuscript is about 4,100 lines of section text. I read its introduction, consequences section and assembly, and only excerpts of the theta and Hecke sections (04, 05), so those proofs are not checked. In the theta section the text disclaims some properties at intermediate parameters (holomorphy; splitting over every unitary group) and works only with the restricted statements. The Weil manuscript's Weil-plane theorem is the same statement Markman claims (Markman 2025 Theorem 1.5.1; Markman 2026 Theorem 1.2), and the text calls its geometric proof 'a detailed treatment of Markman's construction'; the claimed new content is the all-powers step. Its dimension-five case analysis (Types I-IV, remainder cases) is terse. The n < 6 determinant supply (Lemma p3ab:determinant-supply, case 2) is said to come from adding CM elliptic factors, which I did not verify. The abelian-cover manuscript's abstract says 'very general' for the diagonal family, but its Theorem thm:main states that for c <= 1 or d = 0 no exceptional set is needed, so for those cases it claims every smooth parameter. The text also notes that a cited moduli discussion (Gonzalez-Diez-Hidalgo-Leyton, Section 4.2) assumes (m-2)(n-1) > 2, and says its own Section sec:family supplies the needed family, including the genus-zero and elliptic boundary cases. I did not verify that section, nor its positive-genus and sphere character analysis. The K3 manuscript's extension to all periods uses Baire and analytic-set arguments (Lemma specialization:ambient) and a rational period transfer through Buskin's theorem. Its middle sections (double covers, Gauss pencil, the uniruled-threefold comparison) are long and I did not verify them. Its introduction claims more than the abstract: HC and GHC extend to Hilbert schemes and moduli spaces via motivic decompositions. The Sept 10 manuscript is conditional by design; its unconditional content is the equivalence in Theorem main:generic.

entries.what_happened: Only 'The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties' (6 Oct) addresses this. Its Corollary cc:tate claims that for every abelian variety A over a finite field F_q, every r >= 0 and every prime l different from char(F_q), the cycle class map CH^r(A) ⊗ Q_l -> H^{2r}_et(A-bar, Q_l(r))^{G_q} is surjective, where G_q = Gal(F_q-bar/F_q). The same corollary states that numerical equivalence and l-adic homological equivalence coincide on rational algebraic cycles on A-bar. The proof applies Milne's Theorem 7.1 and formulation (0.1) of Milne 1999 ('Lefschetz motives and the Tate conjecture'), with the author's correction. It then passes from geometric cycles to cycles over F_q by a finite pushforward and division by m.
entries.delivers: Tate's first conjecture, in the form stated (surjectivity of the l-adic cycle class map onto the Galois-invariant part, rational coefficients, every codimension, every l different from the characteristic), for all abelian varieties over finite fields. That is the abelian-variety, finite-field case of the bullet's question. It does not reach the general statement for smooth projective varieties over finitely generated fields, and it does not address Tate's second conjecture (rank of algebraic cycles modulo homological equivalence against the order of the pole of the L-function at s = r). The manuscript does not claim to settle the bullet.
entries.remains: Tate's first conjecture for smooth projective varieties over finitely generated fields other than abelian varieties over finite fields, including abelian varieties over number fields, K3 surfaces and other varieties, and the divisor case beyond abelian varieties. Tate's second conjecture, for every variety. Integral and strong (semisimplicity) variants are outside the bullet and are not treated.
entries.direction: proves the conjecture for abelian varieties over finite fields (all codimensions, all l different from p)
entries.conditional_on: Milne's Theorem 7.1 and formulation (0.1) of Milne 1999 (Compositio Mathematica 117), read with the author's correction page (cc:Milne1999Addenda, hosted at jmilne.org; not in the repository). The text says the hypothesis of Milne's theorem is supplied by the paper's own CM Hodge theorem (Theorem thm:cm). No companion manuscript is needed for this corollary.
entries.doubts: The corollary relies on a published theorem of Milne whose auxiliary-field choice the text says needs correcting; the correction is an externally hosted author's note, which I did not read. The text itself says Milne's implication does not assert that each Tate class lifts to a Hodge class on a single CM lift. No step is flagged as sketched in the corollary or its proof.

entries.what_happened: Only 'The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties' (6 Oct) addresses this. Its Corollary cc:standard claims two things for an abelian variety A of dimension g over an algebraically closed field K. First, for every prime l different from char(K), numerical and l-adic homological equivalence coincide on rational algebraic cycles on A. Second, for every rational ample divisor class h and every 0 <= r <= g/2, the rational symmetric form (x,y) -> (-1)^r deg(x y h^{g-2r}) on the primitive kernel P_h^r(A)_Q is positive definite after extension to R. The text calls the second part the Hodge standard conjecture for l-adic cohomology of abelian varieties in arbitrary characteristic. The proof re-applies Milne's Theorem 3.3 of Milne 2002 ('Polarizations and Grothendieck's standard conjectures'), read with Theorem 2.1, Milne's addendum and the 1999 addenda, with the Hodge-type hypothesis supplied by the paper's CM theorem.
entries.delivers: The Hodge standard conjecture (positivity of the form on primitive algebraic classes, modulo numerical equivalence) for abelian varieties over algebraically closed fields in all characteristics, and Conjecture D (numerical = homological equivalence) for abelian varieties, stated with the l-adic homological equivalence for every l different from the characteristic. The problem's list records Wikipedia's status note for D as the Clozel case for infinitely many primes l; this manuscript states the claim for every prime l different from the characteristic, so the judge should check that comparison. Not addressed: Conjectures A and B (Lefschetz type) and Conjecture C (Kunneth type) for any variety, and Conjecture D and the Hodge standard conjecture for smooth projective varieties other than abelian varieties. The manuscript does not claim to settle the full bullet.
entries.remains: Conjectures A, B and C for all smooth projective varieties, and for abelian varieties (not addressed). Conjecture D and the Hodge standard conjecture for smooth projective varieties other than abelian varieties.
entries.direction: proves the Hodge standard conjecture and Conjecture D for abelian varieties (all characteristics)
entries.conditional_on: Milne's Theorem 3.3 and Theorem 2.1 of Milne 2002 (Annals of Mathematics), read with Milne's author addendum to the 2002 paper and the 1999 addenda (both externally hosted at jmilne.org; not in the repository). The Hodge-type hypothesis is supplied by the paper's own CM theorem. The text says this is a re-application of Milne's proof with the same Hodge hypothesis, not a new argument.
entries.doubts: The corollary's correctness depends on Milne's proof and the two cited addenda, which I did not read. The text does not discuss Conjectures A, B or C at all. The abstract says 'the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in arbitrary characteristic', while the corollary states the positivity for l-adic cohomology; I read this as the same claim, stated with l-adic cohomology. No step is flagged as sketched.
